rubriker.title: Samarkand R9 (open): Uzbekistan retake sole lead after beating the US
rubriker._rss_content: Uzbekistan regained sole first place in the Chess Olympiad by beating top seeds United States 2½–1½ in round nine, with Nodirbek Abdusattorov and Nodirbek Yakubboev again providing the decisive points - like they did against China in round seven. India, Armenia and the over-achieving Uzbekistan 2 are one match point behind, the latter after a striking 3½–½ victory over the Netherlands. Two rounds remain in Samarkand. | Photo: Rafal Oleksiewicz / FIDE

rubriker.title: On the Superfluity of Words (3)
rubriker._rss_content: In his essay Christian Hesse - professor of mathematics and, no less importantly, a passionate lover of chess - brings together mathematical and chess problems that are complete and self-contained, problems that explain themselves and need no lengthy verbal instructions. Helmut Pfleger, grandmaster and medical researcher, tells us what he thinks of the subject.

rubriker.title: Uzbekistan Pulls Clear as Gukesh Delivers Mate on Board One
rubriker._rss_content: Two rounds from the finish in Samarkand, the Olympiad has a single leader again. Uzbekistan beat the United States 2.5-1.5 on Thursday, and with Germany losing to India on the next table over, the hosts are alone at the top of the Open section for the first time since the draw that had tied them with Germany in round 8.

rubriker.title: Daniel Rensch: “Maybe I’m the villain to help Hans grow his Endgame.AI business”
rubriker._rss_content: Daniel Rensch discussed the Hans Niemann controversy, his role as its perceived “villain,” and Niemann’s Endgame.AI venture in a recent interview with Mustreader.

rubriker.title: Bodhana Sivanandan Makes History with Final WGM Norm at 11
rubriker._rss_content: Bodhana Sivanandan made history by becoming the youngest-ever player to complete the requirements for the Woman Grandmaster title at just 11 years old.

rubriker.title: Olympiad Day 8 Recap: Germany Blow the Open Race Wide Open
rubriker._rss_content: Germany stunned Uzbekistan to reopen the Open title race, while China seized the lead in the Women’s section with three rounds remaining.

rubriker.title: Call for Emergency ECU General Assembly
rubriker._rss_content: Malcolm Pein has published an open letter to European Chess Union delegates and federation presidents calling ECU President Zurab Azmaiparashvili's endorsement of Wadim Rosenstein "unacceptable," and has moved to trigger a formal accountability process against him, one day before FIDE's own presidential vote.
